### Description

• 7 months ago

I found a stack overflow in the Servo/Stylo CSS parser when processing deeply nested CSS rules. The parser has no recursion depth limit, and when external
stylesheets are loaded asynchronously via <link rel="stylesheet">, parsing runs on rayon thread pool workers with only 256 KB of stack
(STYLE_THREAD_STACK_SIZE_KB at servo/components/style/parallel.rs:33).

Approximately 500 levels of CSS nesting are sufficient to exhaust the stack and crash the content process.

The unbounded recursion occurs in:

  * NestedRuleParser::parse_block() at rule_parser.rs:1019
  * parse_nested() at rule_parser.rs:568
  * These call each other recursively with no depth counter

This affects @media, @supports, @layer, @scope nesting and CSS nesting syntax.

Steps to reproduce:

  1. Serve the attached evil_media_500.css and poc_css_auto.html via HTTP
  2. Open poc_css_auto.html in Firefox
  3. The page loads the CSS via <link rel="stylesheet">
  4. The rayon thread pool worker parses the 500 nested @media rules
  5. Stack overflow -> content process crash

Alternatively, open poc_css_overflow.html for an interactive test with buttons for different nesting depths.

Observations:

  * 500 levels @media nesting via <link>: CRASH (async, 256KB stack)
  * 500 levels CSS nesting via <link>: CRASH (async, 256KB stack)
  * 2000 levels via inline <style>: No crash (main thread, larger stack)

This confirms the crash is specific to the small rayon thread pool stack.

Tested on:

  * Firefox 148.0, Windows 11 Pro
  * Crash is immediate and consistent

Suggested fix: add a nesting depth counter to parse_nested()/parse_block() with a limit around 128. The HTML parser already caps at 511, and the JS parser uses
AutoCheckRecursionLimit.

#### pub fn parse_nested_block<F, T, E>( &mut self, parse: F, ) -> Result<T, ParseError<E>>

where F: FnOnce(&mut Parser<'i>) -> Result<T, ParseError<E>>,

Parse the content of a block or function.

This method panics if the last token yielded by this parser (from one of the `next*` methods) is not a on that marks the start of a block or function: a `Function`, `ParenthesisBlock`, `CurlyBracketBlock`, or `SquareBracketBlock`.

The given closure is called with a “delimited” parser that stops at the end of the block or function (at the matching closing token).

The result is overridden to an `Err(..)` if the closure leaves some input before that point.
